_comment: EXT-63, arm 21 — the 1 h SETTLED-WINDOW grading of arm 20 (canonical + LV-1 + LV-2
+ LV-4, the frame-invariant carry screen).  Counterpart of arm 19 (LV-1+LV-2, no
LV-4), which is the reference this arm is read against.
WHY 1 h IS REQUIRED HERE.  The arm-20 smoke did exactly what the card intended to
the SCREEN -- 1148 of 1219 harvests folded (arm 18: 381), 11 erases on genuine
peer-relative outliers, and the retired frame screen would have withheld 852 of
those same folds (74.2 %) -- but the LEVEL over those 20 epochs got noisier
(mean 39.2 vs arm 18's 25.8 against GIM 32.24, swinging 19.5-61.6).  20 epochs is
inside ignition, where the confounded direction is re-realizing by metres per
epoch; that window cannot separate 'the extra carry information is harmful' from
'ignition is louder when more priors fold'.  The standing rule applies: grade on a
settled window.
PREDICTION, STATED BEFORE THE RUN:
- Fold fraction >> arm 19's 51.9 % -- approaching the harvest count, since the
withheld population was a frame artifact, not receiver health.
- Erase count stays SMALL (order 10-100 over 121 epochs at 61 stations) and the
max robust sigma-hat stays order 1-2 m.  A run where erases climb into the
hundreds means the peer-relative scale is tracking a real per-station
instability, which is a finding about the network, not about the screen.
- a00: the settled second half sits closer to GIM 32.24 than arm 19's (which
ended 33.08 with mean 35.09).  The load-bearing question is the VARIANCE: if
the extra folds mostly carry between-station DIFFERENCE information, the
breathing amplitude should NARROW; if they re-import frame content faster than
LV-2's mu drains it, the amplitude WIDENS and mu grows -- arm 20 already showed
max |mu| 1.96 -> 8.87 m when the folds tripled, so read mu against the fold
count, not on its own.
- If the amplitude widens at 1 h: the honest reading is that the carry's
information is worth admitting only once its common mode is drained on a
per-epoch basis faster than lag-1 -- i.e. the next card is mu's LAG, not the
screen.  Say that rather than re-tightening the screen to hide it.
- Watch the two sigma0 families (the lane A/B lesson): prior side quieter while
the post-fit data side gets louder is OVER-RETENTION, not improvement.
